article_lead.description: the data model with a conventional prior measure whose posterior must be checked for propriety

new_bank_questions.title: Does this reference posterior exist?
new_bank_questions.body: For a Gaussian linear model with the reference measure π(β,σ²)∝1/σ², consider (a) n=5, p=2, full-rank X and residual sum of squares 6; (b) the same n and p but a rank-one X; (c) full-rank X but residual sum of squares zero. In which cases is the posterior proper, and why?
new_bank_questions.answer: Only (a) is proper: n-p=3>0 and the positive residual sum of squares controls the variance integral. In (b), a coefficient direction is unidentified and the flat prior leaves infinite mass. In (c), the variance kernel diverges near zero.

new_bank_questions.title: A reference posterior from three observations
new_bank_questions.body: In an intercept-only normal model, observations are 1, 2 and 3. Under π(β,σ²)∝1/σ², find the fitted mean, residual sum of squares, residual degrees of freedom and inverse-Gamma posterior parameters for σ².
new_bank_questions.answer: The fitted mean is 2 and the squared residuals are 1, 0 and 1, summing to 2. With n=3 and p=1, the residual degrees of freedom are 2. Hence σ² given the data is inverse-Gamma with shape (n-p)/2=1 and scale SSE/2=1. It is proper, but its mean is infinite.
